To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

agroforestry projects that are successful in the long term are those that: 1. are flexible in their management and can respond to changes in the local situation; 2. provide farmers with short term benefits from their participation in the project; 3. involve farmers in all aspects of project management; 4. have the support of local institutions, including local government; and 5. are not dependent upon the continuation of project funds for their survival.

(i) agroforestry projects are more likely to be sustainable when the project design is based on the needs of the farmers, (ii) the project design must include a plan to transfer the technology to the farmer, and (iii) a plan to maintain the project after the formal project ends is essential.

the most sustainable forestry activities are those that involve local people, that are based on technologies that provide obvious benefits to local people in a relatively short period of time, and that are managed by flexible and agile project managers.
